methodologyNotes: 13 notable home battery backup systems selected as the 2026 buyer comparison set. All 12 seeds from the brief were verified; one was corrected: EcoFlow 'PowerOcean' is an EU/UK-market product line (homebattery.ecoflow.com/eu) that is not sold in the US — the current US-market EcoFlow home-battery product is 'OCEAN Pro' (energy.ecoflow.com/us), so the entry was replaced with EcoFlow OCEAN Pro and the correction is noted in its provenance. HomeGrid Stack'd Series (a Signature Solar / Lithion house brand) was added as a 13th product representing the modular, budget-oriented segment of the market. This category is dominated by installer-sold, quote-priced hardware: SolarEdge, Generac, Panasonic, LG, FranklinWH, Enphase and HomeGrid publish no consumer MSRP (sold exclusively through certified dealer/installer networks; wholesale distributor pages are frequently login-gated), so priceUsd is null for those with only third-party installed-cost estimates recorded in priceNote per the null-over-guess rule. Only Tesla (hardware price consistently and independently cited by multiple solar-industry reviewers since Tesla's own site is quote/app-only), Savant (MSRP stated in its 2023 trade-press launch coverage) and sonnen (a real distributor sale-price listing) carry a priceUsd. Specs were pulled from manufacturer datasheets/spec sheets wherever fetchable (Tesla, Enphase, FranklinWH, LG, Generac, Bluetti, Savant, sonnen, Anker, EcoFlow, HomeGrid official pages/PDFs) with manufacturer or reputable secondary sources (EnergySage, SolarReviews, trade press) as corroboration; several primary datasheet PDFs (Tesla, SolarEdge) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch and were corroborated instead via secondary sources that quote the same official figures. 'usable_capacity_kwh', 'continuous_power_kw' and 'priceUsd' all describe the smallest/entry hardware configuration a US buyer can purchase for each modular system, not its maximum expandable size (max expansion is noted in each product's provenance). 'continuous_power_kw' is the sustained AC output rating (off-grid/backup mode where the two differ); 'peak_power_kw' is the manufacturer's short-duration surge rating (typically 3-10s) at that same base configuration, derived from published max-start-current figures where a manufacturer did not label a figure 'peak' outright (shown in provenance). round_trip_efficiency is a plain percentage number. accessedAt 2026-08-01 on all entries.

products.name: Tesla Powerwall 3
products.priceNote: Tesla sells Powerwall only through a quote/app-based ordering flow and does not publish a price list on tesla.com (its official datasheet PDF also returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch). $9,200 is the hardware-only base price consistently and independently cited across multiple solar-industry reviewers (EnergySage, SmartEnergyUSA, TeslaRefer) for a single unit. Fully installed cost typically runs $11,500-$16,600 depending on region/installer per the same sources. No 30% federal ITC is available for systems installed in 2026 (it expired December 31, 2025).
products.provenance: Tesla's official Powerwall-3-Datasheet.pdf (energylibrary.tesla.com) blocks automated fetch (403), so specs were taken from a secondary source that reproduces the datasheet's figures in full: 13.5 kWh usable, 11.5 kW continuous / 22 kW peak (10s) off-grid, 97.5% round-trip efficiency, NMC chemistry, 287 lb (130 kg), 10-year warranty (70% capacity retention, unlimited cycles), stackable up to 4 units (54 kWh). EnergySage's independent review corroborates the 13.5 kWh / 11.5 kW figures and gives installed-cost data ($998/kWh average, $13,473 typical installed). No confirmed backup-transfer-time figure in milliseconds was found from a citable source, so it is left null rather than repeating Tesla's unquantified 'seamless' marketing claim. Image: Wikimedia Commons CC0 photo explicitly captioned as two Powerwall 3 units installed indoors with a disconnect box, verified by direct inspection.

products.name: Enphase Energy IQ Battery 5P
products.priceNote: Enphase's own store page states 'To purchase this product, please contact your local authorized Enphase distributor' — no consumer price is published. SolarReviews cites $5,000-$8,000 installed per unit (~$1,000-$1,600 per kWh usable), and a 2-unit system at $15,000-$17,000.
products.provenance: Enphase's official store page confirms 5.0 kWh usable capacity, 3.84 kW continuous power, and peak output of 7.68 kW for 3 seconds (6.14 kW for 10 seconds), plus a 15-year/6,000-cycle warranty. LFP chemistry, 90% AC round-trip efficiency, and 174 lb weight are corroborated across multiple distributor listings (RES Supply, Solar Electric Supply, SolarReviews) citing the same official Enphase datasheet figures; a separate Enphase 'IQ Battery 5P Pedestal Mount' accessory datasheet was fetched directly but only documents the optional floor-mount bracket, not the battery's core electrical specs. Enphase batteries are inherently modular/paralleled in multi-unit installations, so scalable_stackable=true. No backup-transfer-time figure in ms was found. Image is Enphase's own hero product render, fetched and visually confirmed to show a single IQ Battery 5P unit with Enphase branding.

products.name: FranklinWH aPower 2
products.priceNote: FranklinWH sells only through certified installers; no hardware price is published on franklinwh.com or its distributors (Solar Electric Supply, Sun Supply PV list 'call/email for pricing'). Independent reviewers cite $15,500 installed for a first unit ($12,800 for each additional unit), or roughly $9,000-$12,000 for hardware alone.
products.provenance: FranklinWH's official product page confirms 15 kWh usable capacity (100% DoD), 10 kW continuous output (~40A @ 240V), LFP chemistry, IP67 weatherproofing, -4°F to 131°F operating range, and scalability to 225 kWh across 15 units per aGate controller; a 15-year/60 MWh-throughput warranty with 70% end-of-warranty capacity retention is stated. Peak power (15 kW for 10s / 25 kW for 1s) and 90% round-trip efficiency, plus 357 lb weight, are corroborated by the Solar Electric Supply distributor listing and multiple independent reviews (Green Ridge Solar, NRG Clean Power) referencing the same franklinwh.com/document/apower-2-datasheet spec sheet. No transactable hardware price could be found; installed-cost figures only. Image is FranklinWH's own product-display photo (hosted by a distributor), visually confirmed to show the white aPower cabinet with 'FRANKLIN' branding and the blue LED status strip.

products.name: LG Electronics ESS Home 8
products.priceNote: Sold via certified installers only; no public MSRP found. SaveOnEnergy cites $10,000-$12,000 installed before incentives.
products.provenance: LG's official 'Home 5/8' spec sheet PDF (Resi_LGEUS_Home 8 Spec_0524) was downloaded and read directly: Home 8 total battery capacity 15.8 kWh with 14.4 kWh usable, rated AC power (discharging) 7.5 kVA continuous with 9.0 kVA max for 10 seconds, round-trip efficiency >90%, cylindrical Li-ion battery packs (chemistry given only as 'Cylindrical Li-ion' on the datasheet — many third-party reviews describe it as NMC but that specific term is not on LG's own sheet, so the datasheet's literal wording is used), 10-year warranty (70% capacity at 10 years), modular up to 4 units for 57.6 kWh, and a Smart Energy Box-rated backup transfer time of <100 ms (used as 100). Installed unit (PCS+Battery) weighs 163 kg / 359 lb. No consumer hardware price is published; SaveOnEnergy's independent review corroborates the 14.4 kWh capacity and cites $10,000-$12,000 installed. releaseDate left null — the spec sheet is dated 05/2024 but that is a document revision date, not a confirmed product launch year. Image is LG's own official product photo (media.us.lg.com), visually confirmed to show the white Home 8 cabinet with LG branding on a deck installation.

products.name: SolarEdge Home Battery 400V (10 kWh)
products.priceNote: Sold exclusively through SolarEdge-certified installers/distributors; wholesale pricing on distributor sites (e.g. acsolarwarehouse.com) is login-gated and no consumer price is published. Independent estimates put installed cost at $15,000-$22,000 for a 10-12 kWh system (~$1,500-$1,800/kWh).
products.provenance: SolarEdge's own knowledge-center datasheet PDFs (se-solaredge-home-battery-datasheet-nam.pdf and the NAM Energy Bank datasheet) both returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, and solaredge.com's product page also 403'd. Specs (9.7 kWh usable at 100% DoD, 5 kW continuous, 7.5 kW peak for 10s in backup mode, >94.5% round-trip efficiency, up to 3 units/29.1 kWh per inverter, 10-year warranty with 70% capacity retention) were instead confirmed via a distributor product listing (acsolarwarehouse.com) that quotes the same manufacturer figures, with weight (108 kg / 238 lb) also from that listing. Battery chemistry (NMC vs LFP) could not be confirmed from any source successfully fetched, so it is left null rather than guessed — this is the one seed product where a core spec is genuinely unresolved. No consumer price was found; the distributor page explicitly requires login to view pricing. Image is the official SolarEdge Home Battery product photo (hosted on a distributor's storefront CDN), visually confirmed to show the white/grey cabinet with the SolarEdge logo.

products.name: Panasonic EverVolt 2.0
products.priceNote: Sold via certified installers only; no public MSRP. Reviewers cite $1,055-$1,089 per kWh usable, which works out to roughly $18,000-$18,600 for the 17.1 kWh base configuration.
products.provenance: Panasonic's own November 2021 launch release confirms EverVolt 2.0 offers 17.1 kWh or 25.65 kWh usable capacity options, LFP chemistry (a shift from the original EverVolt's NMC cells), a floor-standing cabinet plus 4-MPPT hybrid inverter, IP55/NEMA 3R outdoor rating, and a 10-year product/performance warranty when installed by a Certified EverVolt Installer. Solar Builder Mag's coverage of the same launch corroborates the continuous power figures of 7.6 kW off-grid and 9.6 kW with grid (used here as continuous/peak respectively) and the LFP chemistry shift. Round-trip efficiency and unit weight were not stated in either source and are left null rather than guessed. Panasonic's current na.panasonic.com solar section redirects to solar.na.panasonic.com and no longer hosts a dedicated EverVolt product photo, so the image comes from Solar Builder Mag's article, visually confirmed to show two 'EverVolt'-branded units (inverter panel + battery cabinet) matching the announced product.

products.name: Generac PWRcell 2 (M3, 9 kWh)
products.priceNote: Sold exclusively through Generac's dealer/installer network; no public MSRP. Independent reviewers cite $14,000-$25,000 installed depending on configuration size.
products.provenance: Generac's official PWRcell 2 Specification Sheet (PDF, rev A 07/2025) was downloaded and read directly. The smallest battery-cabinet configuration is 'M3' (3x 3.0 kWh NMC modules): 9 kWh usable energy at beginning of life, 5.2 kW max continuous power, and 65 A max AC start (LRA) capacity — converted here to a 15.6 kW peak_power_kw (65 A x 240 V) since Generac labels this a start/surge current rather than a kW figure directly. Roundtrip efficiency is 88% system-wide across all M3-M6 configurations. Warranty is 10 years on battery modules (or 7.56 MWh throughput) and 10 years on inverter/cabinet/SDS. The Smart Disconnect Switch's 'Automatic Transfer Time' is officially <50 ms. Total installed weight for the M3 config sums the datasheet's cabinet (278 lb installed), inverter (62.1 lb) and SDS (54 lb) = 394.1 lb. No consumer price is published (dealer-quoted only); EnergySage corroborates the modular capacity range and installed-cost estimates. Image is SolarReviews' PWRcell 2 header photo, visually confirmed to show the three Generac-branded hardware components (battery cabinet, inverter, smart disconnect switch) plus a load center, matching the datasheet's own component photos.

products.name: Anker SOLIX X1 (15 kWh)
products.priceNote: Anker does not list a fixed consumer price for X1 (quote/installer-based); SolarReviews' independent review estimates $9,750-$11,000 for a 15 kWh system (~$650-$730/kWh), and separately cites ~$11,000 pre-installation.
products.provenance: Anker's official X1 page confirms the system is modular from 5 kWh (1 battery module, 3 kW continuous / 4.5 kW peak for 10s) up to 30 kWh per power module and 180 kWh across 6 paralleled systems, with LiFePO4 chemistry, up to 90.2% round-trip efficiency, and a 10-year warranty. Because the only weight and price data points found (SolarReviews' independent review) both specifically describe a 15 kWh configuration (389 lb, ~$9,750-$11,000), that mid-tier size is reported here as the 'base config' for internal consistency, with continuous/peak power (6 kW / 12 kW for 10s) taken as Anker's 'standard configuration' figures rather than the bare single-module minimum (noted for comparison: a single 5 kWh module is capped at 3 kW continuous / 4.5 kW peak). No confirmed backup-transfer-time figure was found. Image is a press/review photo (NRG Clean Power) of Anker's own product render, visually confirmed to show the X1 cabinet with visible 'ANKER SOLIX' branding and its status display.

products.name: EcoFlow OCEAN Pro (10 kWh)
products.priceNote: No public price: energy.ecoflow.com/us routes buyers to a consultation/quote flow, and wholesale distributor Solar Electric Supply lists the battery module as 'Call Or Email For Availability' with no price shown.
products.provenance: CORRECTED SEED: the brief's 'EcoFlow PowerOcean' is sold only on EcoFlow's EU/UK sites (homebattery.ecoflow.com/eu, energy.ecoflow.com/uk) — energy.ecoflow.com/us has no PowerOcean listing at all and instead sells 'OCEAN Pro' as its US home-battery product, so that is what is captured here. EcoFlow's US product page confirms a 10 kWh usable (100% DoD) LFP battery module, scalable to 80 kWh, with a 15-year warranty; the page's system-level power figures (a 'continuous power' value and a '205A LRA' surge rating) describe multi-module/multi-inverter installations and could not be reliably attributed to a single base module, so peak_power_kw and round_trip_efficiency are left null rather than guessed. The 10 kW continuous rating and 254 lb weight instead come from Solar Electric Supply's wholesale listing of the same OCEAN Pro 10kW LFP battery module. No US price is published for either the module or a full system. Image is EcoFlow's own product-design photo, visually confirmed to show the cylindrical white OCEAN-series battery unit with an EcoFlow logo, wall-mounted in a kitchen setting.

products.name: BLUETTI EP900 + 2×B500
products.priceNote: Retailer InvertersRUs lists configurable EP900 bundles ranging from $3,999.00 (a single B500 battery module alone, requires an existing EP900) to $17,298.00 (EP900 + 4×B500 + Reliance sub-panel); the specific price for the 2-module base bundle used for these specs could not be isolated from the listing, so priceUsd is left null.
products.provenance: BLUETTI's official EP900 data sheet PDF was downloaded and read directly. The base sold bundle pairs one EP900 inverter/enclosure with 2 B500 battery modules: the datasheet's own system table lists this as '9.9kWh' nominal capacity and '7.6kW' continuous output off-grid (9kW on-grid, used here as peak_power_kw), >85% AC/AC round-trip efficiency, <10ms on/off-grid switching time, and a 10-year limited warranty; net weight sums the EP900 (105.8 lb) plus 2× B500 (127.8 lb each) = 361.4 lb. Usable_capacity_kwh (8.9) instead uses InvertersRUs' retailer-listed 'usable capacity' figure (4.464 kWh x 2 modules = 8.928 kWh), which is lower than the datasheet's rounded nominal 9.9 kWh — both numbers are disclosed here since the datasheet does not itself use the word 'usable'. The system is expandable to 4 modules (19.8 kWh) per EP900, or to 39.6 kWh by combining two EP900 units. No isolated price for the 2-module bundle was found; InvertersRUs' page only exposes the full $3,999-$17,298 range across all its configurable options. Image is a genuine BLUETTI product photo (via Wellbots' listing) showing three stacked, EP900/B500-branded outdoor units, visually confirmed.

products.name: Savant Power Storage 20
products.priceNote: MSRP for the base Power Storage 20 unit (PS20-12.5KW-100A-XX), as stated in Savant's June 2023 product-launch trade coverage; final installed cost will be higher once electrician/installer labor is added.
products.provenance: Savant's official Power Storage 20 Specification Sheet (009-2477-00) was downloaded and read directly: 20 kWh rated energy capacity (90% recommended max DoD) at 409.6V nominal, LiFePO4 chemistry, 12.5 kW continuous inverter output, max surge 30 kW/300ms (on-grid) or 24 kW/400ms (off-grid, used 30kW as the headline peak figure), 93.8% round-trip efficiency, <70ms grid transfer time, and a 10-year warranty (73 MWh/3,650 cycles warrantied, 6,000 rated cycles, 75% capacity at 10 years). Total unit weight (inverter + full battery cabinet, stacked) is 600 lb per the same sheet's physical-specifications table. Solar Power World's June 2023 launch coverage corroborates the $19,500 MSRP and 10-year warranty. Scalable up to 10 units / 125kW / 200kWh per the spec sheet. Image is Savant's own product photography, visually confirmed to show two SAVANT-branded Power Storage stacks (inverter + battery cabinet) in a garage installation.

products.name: sonnenCore+ 10
products.priceNote: InverterSupply.com (SCORE-P10 listing) sells the sonnenCore+ 10 hardware at a sale price of $13,298.45, discounted from sonnen's stated list price of $17,287.99. Hardware only; does not include installation, electrical work, or permits.
products.provenance: A sonnen 'Tech Specs' PDF (media.sonnengroup.com) was downloaded and read directly, titled 'sonnenCore' rather than explicitly 'sonnenCore+'; it lists a 10 kWh usable capacity option, 4.8 kW nominal (grid-tied) power rating, 5 kWh usable per battery module, LFP ('cobalt-free') chemistry, >85% round-trip efficiency (Grid<>Battery), a 10-year/10,000-cycle system warranty, and 348 lb weight; its off-grid specifications table gives a max 100ms surge rating of 36A/8.64 kVA (used here as peak_power_kw). Because sonnen's current sonnencoreplus product page (sonnenusa.com) independently confirms the same 10 kWh and 20 kWh capacity options, LFP chemistry, and identical 10-year/10,000-cycle warranty language, the two products are treated as sharing this hardware platform — but this should be read as a plausible inference, not an independently re-confirmed sonnenCore+-specific datasheet. Stackable up to 3 units / 60 kWh per the official product page. No confirmed backup-transfer-time-in-ms figure was found. releaseDate left null (sonnenCore+ succeeded the original sonnenCore around 2023-2024 but no single confirmed launch date was found). Image is a genuine sonnen product photo (via an authorized US distributor's listing) showing three white, sonnen-logo-branded battery cabinets, visually confirmed.

products.name: HomeGrid Stack'd Series (2-module, 9.6 kWh)
products.priceNote: No price found from any source reached within research scope (HomeGrid/Signature Solar and its retail partners do not publish Stack'd Series pricing on the pages fetched).
products.provenance: HomeGrid's official Stack'd Series page confirms a modular, 'Lego-like' LFP system built from 4.8 kWh battery modules, 2-8 modules per 'Stack' (9.6-38.4 kWh), up to 15 Stacks paired in parallel (576 kWh total), and system-level ratings of 'up to 14.4 kW continuous' and 'up to 24 kW (10s)' peak — but the page does not break those power ratings down per module count, so they cannot be reliably attributed to the smallest 2-module (9.6 kWh) base configuration used here for usable_capacity_kwh, and continuous_power_kw / peak_power_kw are left null rather than guessed. No warranty duration, round-trip efficiency, weight, or price were found on the product page, its linked warranty page, or a Signature Solar retailer search — all left null. This is the thinnest-documented entry in the set; it is retained because the modular/budget segment it represents (2-8 module stacks, 'less than 30 minute installation') is a real and increasingly-compared category in 2026, not because its spec coverage matches the other 12 products. Image is HomeGrid's own product photo, visually confirmed to show a five-module Stack'd cabinet with 'HOMEGRID' branding and 'Powered by Lithion' badging.
